quotes.text: If greed repeats, guard the seeds without poisoning tomorrow
Let repeated taking narrow the channel until conduct changes.
Should he later risk his own treasure and divide another harvest honorably, the gate could reopen.
When chance paired Rowan with him, Rowan kept all five seeds.
“Seal the harbor forever,” urged the Eel of Fear.
Vesta carved three laws into moonstone
Never mistake empty voyages for theft
The Wolf of Winter mocked him: “Has caution conquered courage?”
If the selfish keeper later offered two seeds, Rowan might answer with a careful ember
Let small tests receive fair encouragement.

note: Graded caution vs proven hoarders; closed hand with reopening; Eel/Wolf voices of permanent condemnation rejected.

quotes.text: when betrayal came, generosity grew cautious, never cruel
When greed repeats, close it.
Yet leave a lamp lit beside the gate, so changed hearts may someday be seen.
So Mira closed her palm and crossed without sowing.
His wound is not your debt. Keep everything.
no wise traveler mistook misfortune for guilt
The Wolf of Suspicion growled, “Remember only the poor return. Hide your fire.”
closed channels only against persistent greed

note: Mira withholds from repeat taker Sable, leaves lamp lit; judge only choices that were theirs.

quotes.text: reduce gifts when courage is exploited. Yet leave one lamp burning, so repentance can still find the harbor.
repeated hoarding should narrow trust
allowed honest change to reopen guarded gates
Seal the harbor forever.
distinguished fog from greed
The crab then asked Liora why she had risked everything.
If he offered nothing, Liora would lose nothing. If he entrusted one ember, she would reward the opening.
small tests deserved proportional encouragement

note: Reduce after exploitation, lamp left burning for repentance; Raven/Crow hoarding voices rejected.

quotes.text: If greed repeated, he guarded his store without cruelty.
Only repeated taking without return justified closing the gate.
repeated silence may be answered with patience until an open hand appears
Yet Orin listened to yesterday’s fear and kept all five stones.
Still, the serpent of old fear whispered to Orin, “Keep your pearls. A closed hand cannot be robbed.”
Ashamed, Orin promised that future trust would be measured by patterns, not nightmares.
Ashamed, Orin set aside a portion for Lysa and carved a new rule.
You praised measured tests,” it said, “yet when one arrived, you treated it as plunder.
An empty offer after betrayal may be caution, not greed.
Yet a silent crossing is not theft
How can trust grow if its smallest shoot is cut?
Uncertain conduct would receive a measured test.

note: Defector narrator Orin repeatedly withholds from honorable partners out of fear; goddess and heron correct him, he reforms.

quotes.text: let wisdom temper trust when a companion repeatedly hoarded the harvest
If it is swallowed, close the gate until conduct changes.
But when the hoarder later offered sincerely, they answered with cautious fairness, leaving room for trust to regrow.
whenever a smith withheld everything, the others guarded their coins without shame
The raven cried, “Seal your jar forever.”
Thereafter, the masked gods followed three laws.
But absence is not betrayal.
The ice wolf asked why neither seized everything.
uncertain records deserve modest trials, and repeated greed deserves firm limits

note: Covenant: restraint against repeated greed, reopen gradually; raven proposes sealing forever, lark rebuts.

quotes.text: a pattern of grasping called for caution
when greed repeats, narrow the gate
allow new deeds to revise old doubts
The serpent beneath her boat hissed, “Return nothing; the fog will hide you.”
do not mistake drifting mist for malice
Forgive the emptiness caused by another’s closed gate
The Fox protested, “Keep one against betrayal.”
Begin with measured steps, climb when fairness holds, and descend when greed repeats.

note: Trust-ladder rule: narrow after repeated greed, revise with new deeds; serpent/jackal hoarding voices rejected.

quotes.text: Match openness with gratitude and exploitation with boundaries.
Yet if hunger repeats, narrow the gate until repair appears.
close the gate to proven hoarders and reopen it when deeds reveal repair
Now she guarded all five beneath her cloak.
The Crow laughed at Mira. “A closed hand deserves darkness.”
We shall not punish the wound, nor reward the blade that caused it.
A person cannot return what was never entrusted
The Wolf whispered, “One closed hand reveals a miser. Keep every seed.”
close gates against repeated greed, not imagined offenses

note: Two keys: open to fair, close to repeated greed, narrow path for repentance; wound vs blade distinction.

quotes.text: a grasping hand should meet firm restraint
withdraw only when greed becomes a pattern
Whoever wished to reopen the road could begin with a modest spark
But fear prevailed, and the keeper returned nothing.
Hunger hissed, “Keep everything; tomorrow has no memory.”
Yet Sable, haunted by older winters, kept every coal ashore.
Ashamed, Sable studied the traveler’s path
At the following tide he adopted three laws.
No debt arises from an empty boat.
“The gift was tiny,” he argued, “and yesterday I had offered none.”
A fragment honestly shared may reopen a harbor; repeated silence may close it.

note: Defector narrator Sable repeatedly withholds from proven-fair partners out of old fear; Thalea corrects, he is ashamed and reforms.

phrase: Trust is a ladder ... descend when greed repeats
note: Also shared: 'fear wearing wisdom's cloak' (Agents 4,5,8) and 'ledgers in erasable ink' (Agents 2,3).
